clue.text: Biting witticism by chap

parts.note: a pun is a play on words, a kind of witticism
gent is short for gentleman, a chap

explanation.surface: A cutting remark made by some man in conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting witticism' reads as one phrase, but 'Biting' alone is the definition and 'by' just places one piece beside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent remark or smell is sharp and stinging, the same figurative sense as biting.

clue.text: Present referee with lawsuit for corruption

parts.note: to put a case is to present it
ref is the usual short form
a legal action is a lawsuit

explanation.surface: Bribing an official in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Corruption in its physical sense is rotting or decay, which is putrefaction.

clue.text: Like Shetlanders, a third Norwegian there, mostly the last of Norsemen

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter goes
a third of a nine-letter word is its first three letters

parts.note: the first three of its nine letters
taken as written, then shortened

indicators.note: the last of a word is its closing letter

parts.note: its closing letter

explanation.surface: Shetland islanders, a good share of them of Norwegian descent from the Norsemen.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shetland Islands are the most northerly part of Britain, closer to Norway than to London.
explanation.definitionFit: Shetlanders live at Britain's far north, so they are northern people.

clue.text: Drawn contest failing to reach conclusion

indicators.note: not reaching the conclusion means the final letter is lost

parts.note: an event is a sporting contest

explanation.surface: A match ending in a tie because it never finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn contest' looks like a single phrase; 'Drawn' alone is the definition, meaning tied.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn game is level, with neither side ahead, so the scores are even.

clue.text: Skin art, worthless stuff as well

parts.note: tat is British slang for cheap, shoddy goods
too means also, as well

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses body ink as cheap rubbish into the bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo is a design inked permanently into the skin, a form of body art.

clue.text: Person often setting skilfully amid sound of derision

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a jeer is a mocking shout
done well is done skilfully

explanation.surface: Someone cleverly fixing things up while being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setting' is not putting a bone or a puzzle but mounting gems in rings and brooches.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeweller's work regularly involves setting stones into metal mounts.

clue.text: Southern sailor, and what he may navigate by?

definitions.note: the whole clue doubles as the definition

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for southern
a tar, or Jack Tar, is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor in southern seas and the guide he steers by.
explanation.walkthrough: Before modern instruments sailors fixed their position by the stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafarers have long navigated by a star such as the Pole Star or the Southern Cross.

clue.text: It's spinning in space curiously free of pathogens

indicators.note: something spinning turns round, so the little word is read from its end back to its start
one piece placed in another means it sits inside that word
curiously suggests an odd, unexpected form, so the combined letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spacecraft tumbling in orbit happens to be germ-free.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and joins the pieces; once the letters are rearranged, the turning of the small word makes no difference to the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic describes conditions that are sterile, with no disease-causing microbes present.

clue.text: Start company 1,000 workers join together?

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
men are workers, as in management and men
to cement things is to bind them together

explanation.surface: A firm launches with a thousand staff joining up.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'join together' is a verb meaning to bond, not workers uniting.
explanation.definitionFit: A commencement is a beginning, the formal word for a start.

clue.text: Gold carried by river in spate

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Gold nuggets washed along by a river in flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In spate' looks like it describes the river, but 'in' only links and 'spate' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden flood or rush, which is what a torrent is.

clue.text: Proposition in article upset Rome

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the city's letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece that stirred up the Italian capital.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a proposition to be proved is called a theorem.

clue.text: Repetition in speech obtrudes

indicators.note: the answer is found within the run of letters across the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Annoying repetition sticks out when someone talks.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated back, so it is a repetition.

clue.text: Gutted keen wise bird with advantage in intelligence

indicators.note: a gutted thing has its insides removed, so only the outside letters stay

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain
the owl is traditionally the wise bird
to have the edge is to have an advantage

explanation.surface: A clever bird, disembowelled, still holds the upper hand in brainpower.
explanation.definitionFit: Intelligence in the sense of information or learning is knowledge, as in gathering intelligence.

clue.text: Retain drink from Japan as souvenir

parts.note: to keep is to retain
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Holding on to a bottle of Japanese liquor to remember the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small object kept in memory of a person or place, much like a souvenir.

clue.text: Limit on activity of disused railway

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a time by which something must be done
second meaning, as two words: a railway line no longer in use is a ...

explanation.surface: Restrictions on work along an abandoned railway track.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadline is a cut-off time that limits how long an activity may continue.

clue.text: Swindle young and vulnerable competitor

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
tender can mean young and easily hurt, as in a tender age

explanation.surface: Cheating an inexperienced, fragile rival.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is someone competing for a title or prize, a rival in the field.

clue.text: Scoff at some of the dire dishes turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
some of means only a part of the following words is taken

parts.note: a run of letters spanning all three words

explanation.surface: Mocking the awful meals being served.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to mock or ridicule, which is to scoff at someone.

clue.text: Unemployed, I would lie vacant

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so the middle is cleared out leaving just the ends

parts.note: only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone out of work admits they would spend the day lying about with nothing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes workers or machines that are not working or employed at the moment.

clue.text: Chewed corn is coating one tooth

indicators.note: a coating wraps around something, so the rearranged letters enclose a piece
chewed food is broken up and mashed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Corn on the cob being eaten leaves a film on a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: Incisors are the flat cutting teeth at the front of the mouth.

clue.text: Ice cream topped cake for afternoon tea

indicators.note: topped means having its top cut off, and in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: a scone is a small plain cake served with jam and cream at British afternoon tea

explanation.surface: A dessert crowned with cake at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topped' looks like decoration on top of a cake, but it means beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice cream bought in a wafer cone is itself called a cone.

clue.text: Old type of word almost completely in the past

indicators.note: almost all of something means its last letter is dropped

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a verb is a kind of word

explanation.surface: An outdated sort of word that has nearly gone out of use.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over is finished and done with, belonging to the past.

clue.text: Bill is able to sing to a good standard

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a statement of money owed

definitions.text: able to sing to a good standard
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words

explanation.surface: A man named Bill turns out to be a decent singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is the request for payment; the second meaning splits the answer into the phrase 'in voice'.
explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill sent to a customer listing goods or services and the amount due.

clue.text: Son running in new leather slippers can't be so?

definitions.note: an adjective phrase: what slippery things cannot be

indicators.note: placed in means set inside the other pieces
running suggests letters moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
kid is soft leather made from young goatskin
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A boy dashing about in new leather slippers that are sure to slide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slippers' are not footwear in the definition but things that slip: anything that slips cannot be non-skid, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-skid means designed not to slide, the opposite of what a slipper (something that slips) does.

clue.text: Serious-minded attention initially needs extremely serious thought

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A grave matter that demands careful consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' reaches forward over all four following words, not back to 'attention'.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest person is sincere and grave in manner, which is to be serious-minded.
